irene.kim: quick question — customer asked what exact acceptance criteria their auditor will need for 'audit evidence' from Redwood (they mentioned SOC2+/FedRAMP-style). they want clear list we can put in contract/SLA. any previous checklist we can reuse?

sam.choi: short answer: auditors want provenance, integrity, and traceability. concrete pieces: event schema, signing, delivery method, retention window, redaction policy, chain-of-custody notes.

punit.desai: for delivery: two patterns we support today: 1) signed bundle (gz + manifest.sig) pushed to S3 with presigned URL + audit manifest; 2) streaming webhook to customer SIEM with TLS + mTLS. which of those do they prefer?

maria.lopez: customer is an enterprise healthcare customer (HIPAA) — legal wants a BAA addendum and a written acceptance criteria doc they can give auditors. they asked for examples of "acceptable evidence file".

kevin.holt: legal note: auditors typically accept either direct artifact delivery (signed bundle) or a certified export with timestamped signature. we should avoid promising <24h delivery unless ops agrees. SLA language must say "delivery within X business days" and list format/crypto expectations.

audit-bot: deploy: evidence-exporter v2.1 completed run for tenant acme-health at 2026-03-18T08:21:09Z (manifest id mfst-0a1b2c).

jordan.lee: can we standardize a single artifact format for all customers? propose: newline-delimited JSON events + top-level manifest.json with keys: signer, signature_alg, manifest_ts, event_count, schema_version, sample_digest. then provide signed manifest (.sig) using Redwood KMS key.

irene.kim: that sounds good. auditor will ask for: 1) full event export (subset allowed if sampling is documented), 2) signed manifest proving integrity, 3) mapping table from event fields -> customer tenancy/RBAC, 4) retention and redaction notes. we need to be explicit on allowed sampling.

sam.choi: example manifest prototype: ```{
  "manifest_id": "mfst-0a1b2c",
  "tenant_id": "acme-health",
  "schema_version": "2026-03-01",
  "events_file": "events-1965432100.jsonl.gz",
  "event_count": 15423,
  "export_ts": "2026-03-18T08:21:09Z",
  "signer": "redwood-kms:projects/rw/keys/evidence-export",
  "signature_alg": "RSASSA-PSS-SHA256"
}```

punit.desai: implementation note: signed with Redwood KMS by default. for customers requiring BYOK/HSM we need a contract clause and a different signing flow (customer-managed key + cross-sign). ops impact estimated 2 sprint work.

maria.lopez: customer specifically asked about FedRAMP-like asks: "do you support signed bundles with FIPS-validated crypto and separated key custody?" they also want proof that events are immutable once emitted.

kevin.holt: answer: we can offer FIPS-mode key store for Private deployments; hosted will support FIPS-signed bundles if we can use a FIPS-validated KMS backend — need infra confirmation. immutability: we can provide hashes and signatures; auditors accept that as long as chain-of-custody is documented.

jordan.lee: RBAC mapping: auditors want to map high-level actions (e.g., model.deploy, secret.rotate, user.grant_role) to an internal actor id + external identity (SCIM/IDP). include mapping CSV with columns: event_field, description, principal_field, idp_claim.

irene.kim: add requirement: record changes to RBAC policies themselves (policy.create, policy.update) and include before/after snapshots in export or point to a snapshot id in manifest.

sam.choi: vuln triage & incident correlation note: if an exported timeframe overlaps with a security incident, include a signed incident appendix with timeline and ticket ids. auditors like consolidated context.

maria.lopez: practical ask from customer: "what turnaround do you promise for ad-hoc evidence requests?" we need a standard: e.g., standard export within 14 business days; expedited (paid) within 3 business days.

punit.desai: 14 business days seems reasonable for hosted given current exports. we can commit to 72 hours for Dedicated/Private with entitlement. add SLA clause: maximum 30 days for archive retrieval if data is cold.

kevin.holt: legal draft bullets to include in contract/SLA: 1) evidence format (JSONL gz + manifest + sig), 2) delivery method and security (S3 presign or SFTP+mTLS), 3) retention window and deletion policy, 4) sampling policy (documented, deterministic sampling only), 5) key custody options (Redwood-managed KMS / customer BYOK), 6) delivery SLAs and fees for expedited exports, 7) limitation of liability and audit scope.

jordan.lee: also call out schema versioning: each manifest must state schema_version and we must publish schema diffs and backward compatibility notes for two prior versions.

irene.kim: next steps: sam/punit to draft a one-page "evidence acceptance criteria" doc we can attach to BAAs/SLAs; kevin to add the legal bullets; maria to confirm customer expedited request; jordan to sketch manifest + mapping CSV examples. can we target a draft by EOD Friday? :calendar:  

sam.choi: acked, will start PR against docs repo.

punit.desai: I'll scope infra work for BYOK export and post an estimate in the thread tomorrow.

kevin.holt: noted — I will draft contract language and share.

maria.lopez: thanks team — I'll update customer that we're preparing a formal acceptance criteria doc and give tentative timelines. :thumbsup: 

audit-bot: note: created ticket SEC-5673 "evidence export SLA + manifest spec" assigned to sam.choi, punit.desai, kevin.holt.

irene.kim: perfect, closing loop here. if anyone sees an auditor edge-case (e.g., required signed timestamp authority), flag it in SEC-5673. :eyes:
